meta.description: Common NCERT Ch 5 Life Processes misconceptions

xylem_phloem_swap.feedback: Xylem transports water and minerals upward; phloem transports food (sucrose) to all parts of the plant.
xylem_phloem_swap.calm_prompt: Ask: is this tube carrying water up or food to storage?

aerobic_anaerobic_confusion.feedback: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen in mitochondria and releases more ATP; anaerobic respiration works without oxygen and gives less energy.
aerobic_anaerobic_confusion.calm_prompt: Check: does this process need oxygen, and where does it happen?

photosynthesis_respiration_swap.feedback: Photosynthesis makes glucose in chloroplasts using light; respiration breaks glucose for energy in all living cells.
photosynthesis_respiration_swap.calm_prompt: Plants do both — but making food and releasing energy are different processes.

autotroph_heterotroph_confusion.feedback: Autotrophs make their own food from CO₂ and water; heterotrophs depend on ready-made organic food from other organisms.
autotroph_heterotroph_confusion.calm_prompt: Who makes the food, and who eats it?

alveoli_nephron_confusion.feedback: Alveoli are air sacs in lungs for gas exchange; nephrons are filtering units in kidneys that form urine.
alveoli_nephron_confusion.calm_prompt: Lungs exchange gases; kidneys filter blood — different organs, different jobs.
